label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Kristen,

Here's the straight story. It was my popcorn and it was my fault.

Saturday, November 7, about 10:40, I put a bag of popcorn in the break room microwave, hit the popcorn button, and walked out front. A customer needed a shear pin for his snowblower and it took longer than I figured, maybe 6 or 7 minutes. By then the bag had burned and the smoke set off the alarm. The store was cleared for about 25 minutes. The engine from up on Hertel came and checked things over. No fire and no damage, just smoke and stink.

That's on me, not the microwave. I walked away from it and I know better.

For the file, the September alarm was not me. That was the sensor in the paint aisle. Saturday was all mine.

I'll cover the $175. Take it out of my check or I'll bring in cash, your call.

I feel bad about everybody standing out in the lot in that cold, and about the Hendersons leaving their cart. They'll be back, they always are, but I'm still sorry it happened.

I'd like to keep my Saturdays if you and Gary will let me. I like the weekend crowd and I need the hours for heating oil. You won't see me near that microwave with popcorn again, any brand.

If it helps, I'm already paying for it. One of the guys on the engine was Mikey Szymanski, who I broke in as a probie back in '03. He will never let me forget this. Thirty-one years on the job, and my first alarm as a civilian is over a bag of butter popcorn. My wife said the van smelled like a burnt movie theater.

Tell Denise I'm buying her coffee.

Walt
